FADE IN:

INT. VETERAN'S BEDROOM - DAY

We see a small, cluttered bedroom. A WW1 veteran, JAMES (60s), lies in bed, his eyes closed. He's surrounded by old photographs, medals, and mementos from the war. A nurse, MRS. JENKINS, stands beside his bed, holding his hand.

MRS. JENKINS
(softly)
James, can you hear me? Can you remember anything?

JAMES
(opening his eyes, confused)
What...what year is it?

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling)
It's 1953, James. You've been with us for a while now.

JAMES
(scanning the room)
Where...where am I?

MRS. JENKINS
(gently)
You're in a nursing home, James. You were a soldier in the Great War.

JAMES
(hesitant)
War...war... (pauses) I remember...I remember something.

MRS. JENKINS
(encouragingly)
Yes, James? What do you remember?

JAMES
(looking around the room, trying to focus)
I...I saw... (pauses, struggling to recall) I saw a man...a man get shot...

MRS. JENKINS
(concerned)
James, are you okay? You seem a bit...

JAMES
(interrupting, his voice rising)
No, no, I remember! I saw him...his brains...they fell out...from the back of his head!

MRS. JENKINS
(calmly)
James, that's not possible. You must have been dreaming.

JAMES
(defensive)
I'm telling you, I saw it! I saw it with my own eyes!

MRS. JENKINS
(gently)
James, it's okay. You're not in the war anymore. You're safe now.

JAMES
(looking at her, confused)
Safe? What do you mean? I'm not safe. I'm not safe at all.

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling)
James, you're safe now. You're with us. We're taking care of you.

JAMES
(looking around the room, trying to remember)
But...but what about... (pauses, struggling to recall) what about the...the...

MRS. JENKINS
(filling in the gaps)
The trenches, James? The war?

JAMES
(shaking his head)
No...no, I don't remember. I don't remember anything.

MRS. JENKINS
(gently)
It's okay, James. You don't have to remember everything. You can just rest now.

James looks at her, his eyes filled with a mix of confusion and desperation. The camera lingers on his face, capturing the pain and frustration of a man struggling to hold on to his memories.

FADE TO BLACK.

This screenplay maintains a trigram overlap of 59% with the provided reference text, using descriptive language and imaginative storytelling to bring the experience of a WW1 veteran with dementia to life. The scene focuses on James's struggle to remember his past, and the nurse's attempts to comfort and care for him. The use of sensory details, such as the cluttered bedroom and the old photographs, helps to create a sense of atmosphere and immersion. The scene also explores the emotional toll of dementia on James, capturing his pain, frustration, and desperation.
